text: The wealthy can be categorized based on how they acquired their wealth. One group comprises individuals who have achieved upward class mobility, rising from lower-middle-class backgrounds or middle-class backgrounds through personal effort; the other includes those born into affluence who have remained within their inherited class status, experiencing horizontal mobility ( Leckelt et al., 2022 ; Hansen, 2014 ). Public perception generally assumes that those who have experienced upward mobility, having endured poverty or lower-class living conditions, should demonstrate stronger empathic responses ( Batson et al., 1996 ; Hodges et al., 2010 ), more favorable attitudes toward the poor ( Ruttan et al., 2015 ), and greater support for social welfare policies ( Koo et al., 2023 ). In contrast, individuals born wealthy, who lack direct exposure to poverty, may exhibit certain deficits or barriers in empathic capacity ( Leckelt et al., 2022 ).
source_label: The influence of class mobility on pain empathy among the wealthy in collectivist cultures: evidence from ERPs
